notes.title: New Features and Maps
notes.content:
[h2]Hello commanders![/h2][p] This month I’ve been working on several improvements that I’d like to share with you.[/p][hr][/hr][h2]🎮 Expanded controller support[/h2][p]I’ve added support for a wider range of controllers so you can play with the gamepad you prefer. I want the tactical experience to feel comfortable from the couch, and I’ll keep expanding this compatibility in future updates.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45558635/db2b469c8e14b6672dbc9513f5274c63e13a99ba.png"][/img][/p][hr][/hr][h2]⚔️ New Local VS Mode[/h2][p]You can now bring a friend! I’ve implemented a [b]local versus mode[/b] for two players on the same screen. Nothing beats recreating WWII battles in strategic duels right from the sofa.[/p][hr][/hr][h2]🌍 New Maps[/h2][p]I’ve also been designing new scenarios that bring more variety both visually and tactically:[/p][list][*][p]🍂 [b]Autumn maps[/b] with colorful forests.[/p][/*][*][p]🪖 [b]Fortifications and trenches[/b] that change how you position your units.[/p][/*][*][p]📦 [b]Environmental details[/b] like crates, barrels, and obstacles that affect combat.[/p][/*][/list][p]These changes make each battle feel different and force you to rethink your strategy.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45558635/86da89437fa93b2e09f100c16c526597330d993e.jpg"][/img][/p][hr][/hr][h2]🚀 What’s next[/h2][p]I’ll continue working on improving animations, adding new units, and adjusting combat balance. I’m also preparing more news about the public demo, which will be available soon.[/p][p]Thank you for supporting the development of [i]A World at War: Tactics[/i]. Your feedback is vital to help this project grow.[/p]

notes.title: Summer Update: Back on the Battlefield
notes.content:
[p]Hey Commanders,[/p][p]I know I’ve been radio silent for a while… truth is, I was going through a bit of a rough patch. Solo development can take its toll sometimes. But I’ve kept working behind the scenes, and I’ve got some exciting progress to share!
[/p][h3]🧠 [b]Smarter Enemies[/b][/h3][p]I’ve been improving the [b]enemy AI[/b] so they make better tactical decisions—taking cover, choosing smarter positions, and coordinating attacks. Flanking them won’t be so easy anymore![/p][h3]
🎶 [b]New Music In the Works[/b]
[/h3][p]I’ve started working on the [b]game’s soundtrack[/b], aiming for something that feels both epic and tactical. Music that enhances the mood of each battle without overwhelming the strategy.[/p][h3]
🛠️ [b]Map Design Mode[/b]
[/h3][p]One of the features I’m most excited about: a [b]Map Design Mode[/b]! Players will be able to build their own battlefields and later use them in [b]Skirmish Mode[/b]. It’s still early in development, but the foundation is in place.

[/p][p]Thanks for sticking with the project. [i]A World at War: Tactics[/i] is a long journey, but every step forward matters. See you on the battlefield![/p]

notes.title: Devlog: Resumen de Mayo – A World at War: Tactics
notes.content:
[h1]Hello Commanders![/h1]

This month has been a bit quieter in terms of public updates, so I wanted to take a moment to explain why — and also show you what I’ve been working on behind the scenes.

[h2]🎨 Still looking for a lead artist[/h2]
I’m still searching for a lead pixel artist to join the project. In the meantime, I’ve been learning pixel art myself to keep things moving. I’m not quite at the quality level the game deserves yet, but this process has helped me explore and test out new ideas.

[h2]🧱 Animation & art progress[/h2]
While still a work in progress, here are some early results from what I’ve been experimenting with:

Infantry idle animation
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45558635/60cc095a37f626f0ae308f7d199082c373904658.gif[/img]

Marching animation
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45558635/c757f5b842e17d67f61efa4a7c3b9781593e73ef.gif[/img]

Explosion effect (including terrain impact)
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45558635/9d3356047bd421d6f415c9399de57e3b51d6765f.gif[/img]

[h2]🧭 Complete overhaul of the units in-game UI[/h2]
This month, I also finished a full redesign of the in-game UI. It’s now much clearer, more readable, and visually consistent with the rest of the game's art. This was a key step to improve the tactical experience and navigation during combat.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45558635/fb22acecc341f4414e9eaab4b34eaf6c82f9daa1.png[/img]

Thank you for following the development of A World at War: Tactics. Progress might be a bit slower, but the project is still very much alive and moving forward. See you in the next devlog!

Michael

notes.title: No Artistic Reinforcements For Now... But We're Still In The Fight
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45558635/390fae47721ba2b1022c0b1ca6f6c06febac6b73.png[/img]

[h1]Hello, Commanders![/h1]

This week has been a bit unusual: our lead artist has had to step away temporarily, so we won’t have new sprites for now. But don’t worry! Development is still moving full speed ahead, and here are the updates:

[h2]⚔️ Combat Rebalance[/h2]
[b]Damage vs. Defense:[/b] We adjusted the formulas so light units (infantry) aren’t wiped out by a single artillery shot, while heavy weapons still retain their tactical impact.  
[b]Cover and Terrain:[/b] We added minor penalties in difficult terrain (mud, ruins) and +20% defense bonuses in fortifications and trenches.

[h2]🔄 Improved Turn System[/h2]
[b]Turn Order Bar:[/b] We added a visual indicator showing the current unit, the next unit, and the one after, so you can plan your tactics in advance.

[h2]🏰 Fortification System[/h2]
[b]Construction and Repair:[/b] The combat engineer can build light trenches and fortifications and repair them.  
[b]Scalable Durability:[/b] Each fortification has 3 levels; leveling up increases its defense bonus from +10% → +15% → +20%.  
[b]Interactive Use:[/b] Units can now “anchor” to fortifications to receive additional fire and cover bonuses, represented by a small icon over the sprite.

[h1]Next Milestones[/h1]
[list]
[*]Internal playtest of combat and fortification adjustments to fine-tune the numbers.  
[*]Implementation of basic fortification animations (soldier placing sandbags, etc.) — this may take a bit longer while we find a new artist.  
[*]Active search for a new artist or external collaborator to resume sprite work without losing momentum.  
[/list]

Thank you for your unwavering support! Even without art reinforcements, your patience and feedback are helping us forge a solid tactical game.

— Michael

notes.title: Devlog: Details Matter
notes.content:
[h1]Hello, Commanders![/h1]

This week we focused on improving the moment-to-moment feel and visual clarity of the game. These might seem like small tweaks, but they make a big difference in the overall experience:

[h2]❤️ Redesigned Health Indicator[/h2]
Each unit now displays a visible health icon on the battlefield. We wanted something clean, integrated with the art style, and easy to read at a glance. It’s a small change… but it adds a lot of life to the battlefield!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45558635/48d1eb528ce9caab6c613eaf3eb619bcd23f785d.jpg[/img]

[h2]📍 Tactical Facing System[/h2]
In a tactical game, knowing which direction your unit is facing is crucial. This week we implemented a new visual system that lets you choose the unit’s final orientation after moving. It's not only great for planning flanks and ambushes — it also brings that classic tactical flavor we love.
(And yes, watching the arrows spin in real time is oddly satisfying 😄)
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45558635/65cd2ab3d6677d1ec548fd933cb2c5f373284f03.gif[/img]

[h2]🎨 New Sprites and Animations[/h2]
We gave the M4 Sherman a proper makeover! This new sprite brings more definition and personality to one of the most iconic tanks of WWII.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45558635/16c4f62de5e0a8c67b86cd03bf17d5708cfd3822.png[/img]

We’re also introducing a brand-new sprite for a light artillery unit, complete with two soldiers in action.[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45558635/a1106fe96e5348f1485026662f925e2ccda7461d.png[/img]

The new Panzer IV now looks sharper, more menacing, and better aligned with the game’s overall pixel art style.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45558635/2db358156d80fd0f35f2db6bec7887b8f732d11d.gif[/img][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45558635/4070f928bdf66de18b7f59796adbf0a2066ef754.gif[/img]

These visual upgrades help us give each unit more personality. They’re not just pawns in combat — they tell their own story just by standing on the map.

Thank you for following our journey each week. We're building something special, step by step — and you're a key part of that process.
See you on the next devlog!

notes.title: Devlog: Steam SDK Integration, New Animations, and Achievements!
notes.content:
[h1]Greetings, commanders![/h1]

This week, we’ve made some exciting progress behind the scenes, and we’re thrilled to share the latest updates for A World at War: Tactics. Here’s a breakdown of what’s new:

[h2]Steam SDK Integration[/h2]
We’ve successfully integrated the Steam SDK into the game, bringing Steam features like achievements,  and other platform-specific functionalities directly to A World at War: Tactics. This is a major step toward preparing the game for Steam’s release, ensuring that all the necessary features are in place to enhance the player experience.

[b]What does this mean for you?[/b]

Steam Features Incoming: Soon, you'll be able to enjoy all the benefits Steam offers, from achievements to Steam Workshop support, making your experience even more immersive!

[h2]New Animations: Bringing Your Units to Life![/h2]
We’re working hard on implementing new animations for the units to make their movements feel more dynamic and natural. Whether they’re walking, attacking, or reacting to the environment, these new animations will add more life to the battlefield and give you a more immersive experience.

[b]What does this mean for you?[/b]

More Fluidity: Expect smoother, more realistic animations that will make each unit’s actions feel more impactful and visually engaging.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45558635/95b739303d8ba1b6a6c8691306a4405f2b016ba1.gif[/img][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45558635/d9d783084d5000d50126f96fa37c6c2d745948fd.gif[/img]

[h2]Achievements Added: Progress and Rewards![/h2]
This week, we’ve also added the first set of achievements into the game. These are now fully integrated into the game’s code, and as you progress, you’ll be rewarded with unique achievements that track your success and milestones.

[b]What does this mean for you?[/b]

Track Your Progress: As you advance through the game, these achievements will give you a sense of accomplishment and recognition for your strategic victories.

Thanks for your continued support, commanders.
We’re excited to continue improving the game, and these updates are just the beginning. Stay tuned for more! We’ll see you on the battlefield!

notes.title: More Character, More Strategy! Graphic and Gameplay Updates
notes.content:
[h1]Greetings, commanders![/h1]

This week, we've been working hard to improve the gameplay experience in A World at War: Tactics, and we're excited to share our progress with you. Here's a summary of the most important changes:

[h2]New Graphic Style: A Bigger, Easier-to-Animate Chibi Style![/h2]
We've redesigned the game's units to feature a bigger chibi style. This not only makes them more visible on the battlefield but also makes animation easier. The larger heads and compact bodies now allow for greater expressiveness and movement. This change will improve visual clarity, especially at smaller resolutions and when units are deployed on the terrain.

[b]What does this mean for you?[/b]
More charismatic characters and smooth animations that will immerse you further into the action!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45558635/48ab5b8a55f7d4e2d9d2b1ee082bbef9f7b68322.png[/img]

[h2]UI Improvements: Detailed Terrain Information at Your Fingertips[/h2]
We've made significant improvements to the user interface to provide you with clearer and more accessible terrain information. Now, when you approach a battlefield area, you'll be able to see more precise details about defense, terrain type, and other key attributes that will affect your combat tactics.

[b]What does this mean for you?[/b]

[b]Improved Terrain Visualization: [/b]You can now quickly identify how the terrain affects units, whether by providing cover, hindering movement, or altering defense points.

[b]Real-Time Terrain Stats:[/b] When you select a tile, you'll see a detailed summary of the terrain, including its type and the effects it has on units in that area.

[b]Intuitive Interface:[/b] We've optimized the design to make terrain information easy to read without interfering with the action on the battlefield. Now, you can make more informed decisions without distractions!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45558635/3e5071f280c12f3d631640f54634b2b3096355b6.png[/img]
[h2]Gameplay Updates[/h2]
As part of our gameplay improvements, we're introducing new support units: Medical Units and Combat Engineers. These units will play a crucial role on the battlefield, offering unique abilities to strengthen your strategy.

[b]Medical Units: [/b]They will be able to heal wounded units, keeping your fighting force in the fight for longer. Don't let your soldiers fall behind!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45558635/6441ffc7fee7bf274396508792be746f60687a8a.png[/img]

[b]Combat Engineers:[/b] Specialized in repairing vehicles and fortifications, combat engineers will be able to fix damaged units and build structures to reinforce your defense.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45558635/290f7f1a9313b9e1ef42bf580d1c84bd10af2fd8.png[/img]

These new units will provide an additional layer of strategic depth, allowing you to adapt your tactics to the battlefield's circumstances.

[b]What does this mean for you?[/b]
Now you'll have new ways to manage your army, ensuring your troops stay on their feet and ready for action.

Thanks for your continued support, commanders.
This is just the beginning of the major improvements we have planned. See you on the battlefield!

notes.title: Devlog: Reworking the Combat System
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45558635/e5fcc58cfbe3ba947c7a2e4849bdefd800877ac4.gif[/img]
[h1]Greetings, Commanders![/h1]
In this update, we want to share an important improvement to the combat system. After several tests and adjustments, we have reworked how unit engagements are calculated to make battles more strategic and balanced.

Now, damage is determined by the following formula:

[h3]((Attacker’s Health × Unit Type Multiplier) − Adjustment Value) / 2[/h3]

[h2]📌 What does this mean in practice?[/h2]
✔️ The attacker’s health influences the damage they can inflict.
✔️ The multiplier factor depends on the unit type, reflecting strengths and weaknesses.
✔️ The adjustment value balances the damage to prevent imbalances.
✔️ The final result is divided by 2 to keep values more controlled and prevent battles from being too explosive.

[h2]Why this change?[/h2]
We aim for a system that rewards tactical positioning and strategic unit choices. With this new formula, factors like unit type advantage and the attacker's remaining health play a more significant role in battle.

[h2]What’s next?[/h2]
We are still working on how fortifications and unit positioning will impact combat. We want terrain and strategy to play a key role, so the system will likely continue evolving in future updates.

We’re looking forward to your feedback to keep refining the game's balance and tactical depth. Thank you for your support, and stay tuned for more updates! 🚀
